subject: Next steps & proposed sprint plan for Luminar eval
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Barnes <elliot.barnes@luminar.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps & proposed sprint plan for Luminar eval

Hi Elliot — great to meet earlier. Quick recap + a concrete proposal so we can lock schedule and owners.

Recap (from today’s discovery)
- Goal: reduce false positives on content classification and speed up inference latency for customer-facing inference calls.
- Primary constraints: limited labeled data (~20k examples), strict security reviews, target latency for 95th pct <= 300ms.
- Stakeholders you mentioned: Sarah Kim (ML), Rahul Desai (Security), you (CTO) — thanks.

Proposed evaluation plan (4-week sprint)
1) Kickoff week (Day 0): 60–90 min kickoff to align success metrics, access, and environment.
2) Week 1: Data onboarding + baseline run (Redwood runs baseline on current model).
3) Week 2: Config & quantization tuning, batching profile, KV cache setup.
4) Week 3: Load validation & gated integrational checks (throughput/latency).
5) Week 4: Readout + handoff — final metrics, recommended config, cost estimate.

Success criteria (proposed)
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency < 300ms in your test harness.
- Throughput: support sustained 100 req/s on dedicated pool without error spikes.
- Quality: classification F1 >= 0.85 vs your labeled holdout.
- Ops: runbook for dataset refresh and a clear rollback policy.

Owners (suggested)
- Luminar: Elliot (exec), Sarah Kim (ML owner), Rahul Desai (security contact)
- Redwood: Jonas Weber (eng lead), Camila Reyes (solutions SE), Naomi Feldman (onboarding PM)

Immediate asks / next steps
- Can you confirm the success criteria above or propose edits by EOD Thursday (2027-09-23)?
- Please share an S3/Drive link with the dataset and a sample inference harness by 2027-09-24 so we can validate access and format.
- Rahul — if you can point us to the internal security questionnaire owner, we’ll assemble SOC2 evidence and network docs.

Logistics
- Proposed kickoff: Tue 2027-09-28, 10:00 PT.
- Weekly 30-minute check-ins (Fridays) and one final 60-minute readout.

Attaching: POC-success-metrics.xlsx (stub), Mutual_Action_Plan.docx (stub).

Thanks — I’ll draft a mutual action plan and send a calendar invite once we confirm kickoff.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Elliot Barnes <elliot.barnes@luminar.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@luminar.ai>, Rahul Desai <rahul.desai@luminar.ai>
Date: 2027-09-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & proposed sprint plan for Luminar eval

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. Quick responses inline and a few asks from our side.

Appreciate the 4-week plan; that timeline works for us in general. A couple notes:
- Quality metric: we’d prefer to target recall >= 0.85 on the high-risk class (false negatives are costly for us). If F1 is simpler for you, we can accept that but want recall tracked independently.
- Security: Rahul will lead the questionnaire. I’ve CC’d him and Sarah (ML) so they’re looped.
- Data: I can share a redacted dataset; we’ll need an NDA addendum for PII fields (should be small).
- Budget: we have limited pilot credits — can you include an estimated cost range for the dedicated pool (4 weeks) in the mutual action plan? That’s a strong gating item for procurement.

I’ll confirm stakeholder availability and expect to share the dataset link by EOD Friday 2027-09-24.

Subject: Re: Next steps & proposed sprint plan for Luminar eval — internal ops checklist

Team — I put together an internal task checklist to ensure we hit the 4-week cadence. High level:

Week 0 (pre-kickoff, by 9/24)
- Confirm dataset access & sample run (Jonas) — due 9/24
- Security packet (SOC2 + network diagram, Naomi to own collating) — due 9/24
- Provision dedicated pool estimate + cost range (Marissa) — due 9/24

Week 1
- Data validation & schema check (Camila)
- Baseline runs & measurement harness (Jonas)

Week 2
- Quantization and batching experiments (Camila + Jonas)
- Monitor quality drift and log samples (Naomi)

Week 3
- Load validation and chaos checks (Marissa)
- Final parameter tuning and stability runs (Jonas)

Week 4
- Readout prep & slide deck (Naomi)
- Handoff doc and runbook (Camila)

Other notes
- Weekly check-ins: Fridays 30 minutes (status/blocks).
- Final readout: 60 mins (metrics, config, cost).
- I’ll assemble an onboarding-runbook.md stub (attached) with infra commands and expected outputs.

If nobody objects I’ll start creating the runbook and a short checklist we can share with Luminar at kickoff.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Elliot — if you want us to spin a dedicated pool, please confirm expected sustained request rate so Marissa can finalize the cost estimate.

If the agenda looks good I’ll share a more detailed mutual action plan doc and the invite.
